newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Viasa's future to be decided Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Viasa's future to be decided Jan 31.

text.p: The future of struggling Venezuelan airline, Venozolana Internacional de Aviacion SA (Viasa), will be finally decided on January 31 when shareholders will vote whether or not to declare the carrier bankrupt, company sources said.
"Although the hour hasn't yet been set, what is certain is that the meeting has been brought forward due to the grave emergency," one company source told Reuters.
When Viasa grounded all flights last week, the company's executive board originally set the extraordinary shareholders' meeting for February 8.
"But we decided waiting 15 days until February 8 was too long," Viasa commercial director, Juan Pedro Aritio, told leading local daily El Universal.

Venezuela's National Investment Fund president Alberto Poletto, with portfolio for privatization, is currently in Madrid for a second day of talks with the Spanish government to try and save the airline.
State-owned Spanish carrier Iberia holds the largest stake in Viasa with 45 percent, Venezuela holds a 40 percent share, and Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial owns 15 percent.
Viasa had a $30 million loss last year and has not reported a profit since Iberia took over management in 1991.
